stem: A nurse is performing oropharyngeal suctioning with a suction catheter for a client who cannot clear secretions. Which technique is appropriate?

options.A: Apply suction continuously while advancing the catheter into the oropharynx.
options.B: Apply suction during insertion and maintain it until the catheter is fully removed.
options.C: Insert without suction, apply intermittent suction while withdrawing, limit the suction pass to 10 to 15 seconds, and reassess before repeating if needed.
options.D: Continue repeated passes without allowing recovery or reassessing oxygenation when secretions remain.

rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills instructs that suction should not be applied while the catheter is inserted. During withdrawal, suction is applied intermittently, and each suction pass should be limited to 10 to 15 seconds to reduce tissue trauma and respiratory complications. The client's respiratory response should be reassessed between passes, with recovery time before another pass when clinically indicated. C is therefore correct.
educational_objective: Perform catheter-based oropharyngeal suctioning without suction during insertion, use intermittent suction during withdrawal, keep each pass brief, and reassess the client between passes.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf)
source_document_title: Nursing Skills — Chapter 22: Tracheostomy Care & Suctioning
source_version_date: Current NCBI Bookshelf nursing-skills chapter; accessed 2026-08-16
source_locator: 22.4 Oropharyngeal and Nasopharyngeal Suctioning Checklist — steps 22-26: insert without suction; intermittent suction during withdrawal; no more than 10-15 seconds; reassess and allow recovery between passes
source_claim_supported: For catheter-based oropharyngeal suctioning, do not apply suction during insertion; apply intermittent suction during withdrawal, limit each pass to 10-15 seconds, and reassess/recover between passes.

source_original.stem: A nurse is performing oral suctioning for a client unable to clear their own secretions. Correct technique includes:

options.A: Apply continuous suction while inserting and withdrawing the suction catheter
options.B: Advance the catheter deeply while applying continuous suction during insertion
options.C: Apply intermittent suction during withdrawal, keep each pass brief, and reassess
options.D: Perform only one suction pass even when secretions remain after reassessment

source_original.rationale: Correct oral suctioning technique involves applying suction intermittently, primarily during catheter withdrawal, limiting each pass to a brief duration to minimize mucosal trauma and hypoxia, and reassessing the client's respiratory status and secretion clearance between passes, repeating as needed.
source_original.source_detail: Apply suction intermittently during withdrawal; limit suction pass to 10–15 seconds and reassess; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Specified catheter-based oropharyngeal suctioning so the insertion/withdrawal technique is exact, directly verified the 10-15-second limit and reassessment steps, and replaced the weak one-pass distractor with a clinically relevant no-recovery error.

audit_findings.source_authority: NCBI Nursing Skills; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: Current NCBI checklist remains available and directly addresses oropharyngeal suctioning.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Checklist steps directly support no suction on insertion, intermittent suction on withdrawal, 10-15-second limit, and reassessment/recovery between passes.

distractor_audit.B: Same unsafe continuous-suction error during insertion.
distractor_audit.D: Repeated passes without recovery/reassessment conflict with the checklist.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Yankauer oral suctioning uses a different device technique; the final stem explicitly specifies an oropharyngeal suction catheter, resolving that potential ambiguity.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are suctioning techniques within the same procedure.
audit_findings.blueprint: Basic Care and Comfort retained for direct nonpharmacologic secretion-clearance care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the exact checklist lines for insertion, withdrawal, pass duration and reassessment; identified the original 'oral suctioning' ambiguity with Yankauer use, corrected the stem to catheter-based oropharyngeal suctioning, and confirmed C remained uniquely correct.
